q: An object that moves in a circle at constant speed $v$ is said to experience _____ circular motion.
e: An object that moves in a circle at constant speed v is said to experience uniform circular motion. Uniform here means constant speed along the circle. nonuniform or linear is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: In uniform circular motion, the magnitude of the velocity remains constant, but the _____ of the velocity continuously changes.
e: In uniform circular motion, the magnitude of the velocity remains constant, but the direction of the velocity continuously changes. On a circle the velocity direction keeps turning even if the speed is steady. speed or mass is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: The change in direction of velocity constitutes an _____.
e: The change in direction of velocity constitutes an acceleration. Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity, written a or α. force or inertia is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: An object revolving in a circle is continuously accelerating, even when the _____ remains constant.
e: An object revolving in a circle is continuously accelerating, even when the speed remains constant. Speed is the magnitude of velocity. direction or velocity is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: Average acceleration has been defined as $\frac{\Delta v}{\Delta t}$ where $\Delta v$ is the change in velocity during the time interval _____.
e: Average acceleration has been defined as (Δ v)/(Δ t) where Δ v is the change in velocity during the time interval Δ t. Δ s or Δ θ is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: If $\Delta t$ approaches zero, $\Delta v$ will be essentially perpendicular to both velocities and points toward the _____ of the circle.
e: If Δ t approaches zero, Δ v will be essentially perpendicular to both velocities and points toward the centre of the circle. The centre of the circle is where a_C and F_c point. edge or tangent is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: The acceleration directed along the radius towards the centre of the circle is denoted by $a_c$ and is called centripetal acceleration or _____ acceleration.
e: The acceleration directed along the radius towards the centre of the circle is denoted by a_c and is called centripetal acceleration or radial acceleration. Centripetal acceleration a_C points to the centre of the circle and has magnitude v²/r or rω². tangential or linear is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: For uniform circular motion, the centripetal acceleration vector points towards the centre while the linear velocity vector is _____ to the path.
e: For uniform circular motion, the centripetal acceleration vector points towards the centre while the linear velocity vector is tangential to the path. Tangential means along the tangent to the circular path. radial or parallel is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: Hence, the centripetal acceleration and linear velocity are _____ to each other at every point in the path.
e: Hence, the centripetal acceleration and linear velocity are parallel to each other at every point in the path. Parallel would mean along the surface; the road reaction is instead normal to it. perpendicular or equal is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: In nonuniform circular motion, an object is moving in a circular path with a _____ speed.
e: In nonuniform circular motion, an object is moving in a circular path with a varying speed. In nonuniform circular motion the speed changes, so both a_C and a_T are present. constant or zero is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: In nonuniform circular motion, the angular speed of the object is changing and the object experiences the angular _____.
e: In nonuniform circular motion, the angular speed of the object is changing and the object experiences the angular acceleration. Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity, written a or α. displacement or velocity is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: This angular acceleration gives rise to the _____ acceleration which is tangential to the circle.
e: This angular acceleration gives rise to the tangential acceleration which is tangential to the circle. Tangential means along the tangent to the circular path. centripetal or radial is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: In nonuniform circular motion, there is tangential acceleration in addition to _____ acceleration.
e: In nonuniform circular motion, there is tangential acceleration in addition to centripetal acceleration. Centripetal means toward the centre of the circle. linear or gravitational is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: Thus, an object in nonuniform circular motion has a resultant acceleration that is the vector sum of the centripetal and _____ accelerations.
e: Thus, an object in nonuniform circular motion has a resultant acceleration that is the vector sum of the centripetal and tangential accelerations. Tangential means along the tangent to the circular path. radial or gravitational is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: Unlike tangential acceleration, centripetal acceleration is present in both uniform and _____ circular motion.
e: Unlike tangential acceleration, centripetal acceleration is present in both uniform and nonuniform circular motion. Tangential acceleration a_T lies along the tangent and changes the speed along the circle. linear or projectile is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: The two acceleration vectors $a_c$ and $a_T$ are perpendicular to each other, with $a_c$ in the radial direction and $a_T$ in the _____ direction.
e: The two acceleration vectors a_c and a_T are perpendicular to each other, with a_c in the radial direction and a_T in the tangential direction. Tangential means along the tangent to the circular path. centripetal or vertical is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: The magnitude of resultant acceleration $a$ is the square root of the sum of the squares of $a_c$ and _____.
e: The magnitude of resultant acceleration a is the square root of the sum of the squares of a_c and a_T. v or ω is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: In uniform circular motion, an object is continuously accelerating because the direction of the _____ continuously changes.
e: In uniform circular motion, an object is continuously accelerating because the direction of the velocity continuously changes. In uniform circular motion the speed is constant, but velocity still changes direction so a_C is present. speed or mass is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: A rigid body is a body that does not deform, meaning no matter how the body moves, the distance between any two _____ within the body remains constant.
e: A rigid body is a body that does not deform, meaning no matter how the body moves, the distance between any two forces within the body remains constant. Several real forces can add to give the net centripetal requirement. axes or particles is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: Some examples of rotational motion include the motion of the blades of a fan, and motion of a _____ in an amusement park.
e: Some examples of rotational motion include the motion of the blades of a fan, and motion of a Ferris wheel in an amusement park. car or pendulum is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: During time intervals when an object speeds up or slows down, its angular velocity is changing therefore it has an angular _____.
e: During time intervals when an object speeds up or slows down, its angular velocity is changing therefore it has an angular acceleration. Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity, written a or α. displacement or radius is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: The kinematic equations for rotational motion can be derived in terms of the angular displacement, angular velocity and angular _____ of the object at any instant of time.
e: The kinematic equations for rotational motion can be derived in terms of the angular displacement, angular velocity and angular acceleration of the object at any instant of time. Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity, written a or α. mass or force is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: The triangle formed by the radius and arc in circular motion is geometrically _____ to the vector triangle of the change in velocity.
e: The triangle formed by the radius and arc in circular motion is geometrically similar to the vector triangle of the change in velocity. perpendicular or dissimilar is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: Note that the two acceleration vectors $a_c$ and $a_T$ are perpendicular to each other, and the resultant acceleration points at an _____ between $a_c$ and $a_T$.
e: Note that the two acceleration vectors a_c and a_T are perpendicular to each other, and the resultant acceleration points at an intersection between a_c and a_T. axis or angle is a different idea, so those options are wrong.

q: The platter of the hard drive of a computer uniformly rotates, meaning it experiences _____ circular motion.
e: The platter of the hard drive of a computer uniformly rotates, meaning it experiences uniform circular motion. Uniform here means constant speed along the circle. nonuniform or linear is a different idea, so those options are wrong.
